settings.label: Project ID
settings.meaning: Names the Stytch environment: the user name of every API call, the audience of its session JWTs and part of their issuer. A live project id calls https://api.stytch.com; any other calls https://test.stytch.com.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Project ID & API keys, for the environment (Test or Live). Each environment has its own project id, secret and public token.

test.because: This is a Live project id (project-live-…): use the Test environment's project id. The prefix is how Stytch's own SDKs tell Live from Test.

production.because: Production needs the Live environment's project id, which starts with project-live-. The prefix is how Stytch's own SDKs tell Live from Test.

settings.label: Secret
settings.meaning: The password of every API call (HTTP Basic, with the project id). Server-side only.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Project ID & API keys › Secrets, for the same environment as the project id.

settings.label: Public token
settings.meaning: Stytch's frontend SDKs authenticate with it, and the OAuth start URL carries it. Safe in a browser.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Project ID & API keys › Public tokens, for the same environment as the project id.

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from Stytch. Stytch sends its webhooks through Svix, signed with the endpoint's secret (whsec_…).
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Webhooks › the endpoint › Signing Secret.

operations.name: sessions.jwks
operations.purpose: Reads the keys that sign the project's session JWTs, to check them locally. Keys rotate about every six months; both are served for a month. Needs no credentials.

operations.name: sessions.authenticate
operations.purpose: Checks a session token or session JWT with Stytch, so a revoked session fails at once; returns the session, the user and a fresh session JWT.

operations.name: sessions.revoke
operations.purpose: Ends a session, by its id or token. Its JWTs still pass a local check until they expire (five minutes).

operations.name: passwords.authenticate
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with their email and password, starting a session.

operations.name: passwords.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user with an email and password.

operations.name: passwords.resetStart
operations.purpose: Emails the user a link to reset their password; the link carries the token for passwords.reset.

operations.name: passwords.reset
operations.purpose: Sets a new password with the token from the reset email.

operations.name: otps.emailLoginOrCreate
operations.purpose: Emails a one-time passcode, creating the user when the address is new.

operations.name: otps.authenticate
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with the passcode, by the email's id (email_id), starting a session.

operations.name: oauth.start
operations.purpose: Where the browser is sent to sign in with Google or GitHub (a redirect, never called by the server). Query: public_token, login_redirect_url, signup_redirect_url, code_challenge, provider_login_hint.

operations.name: oauth.authenticate
operations.purpose: Exchanges the token Stytch put on the redirect, with the PKCE verifier, for a session.

operations.name: users.search
operations.purpose: Finds users by a query, such as an exact email address.

operations.name: users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user with an email and no password.

operations.name: users.update
operations.purpose: Changes a user's name, metadata or external id.

signature.description: Sent through Svix. svix-signature is a space-separated list of v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "<svix-id>.<svix-timestamp>.<raw body>">, keyed with the base64 after whsec_ in the endpoint's secret. svix-timestamp is Unix seconds; refuse one more than five minutes from now. The body has no type field: the event type is source.object_type.action, lowercased (direct.user.create).

events.meaning: A user was created through the API or an SDK (a sign-up).
A user was changed through the API or an SDK.
A user was deleted through the API or an SDK. The body has the user's id, not the user.
A user was created in the Dashboard.
A user was changed in the Dashboard.
A user was deleted in the Dashboard.
